stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Meta Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model released under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.
It is specifically designed for local coding agents and is optimized via Ollama's MLX engine with new DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: Sam Altman says OpenAI won’t go public until its models are safe
stories.author: Hayden Field
bullet_points: Sam Altman stated that OpenAI's IPO timeline is contingent upon achieving greater model safety.
The decision to delay going public is directly linked to the increasing capabilities and associated risks of their AI models.
No firm timeline has been provided for when OpenAI expects to meet the necessary safety benchmarks for a public offering.

stories.title: OpenAI launches Dots, its Muse competitor
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: OpenAI is launching 'Dots,' a new line of always-on, agentic AI assistants.
Dots is positioned as a direct competitor to Meta's Muse AI.
The assistants will operate across connected apps in the background, learning user preferences, and are powered by GPT-6 Astra.

stories.title: AMD acquires World Labs AI startup, upping the ante against Nvidia
stories.author: Samuel Axon
bullet_points: AMD is acquiring World Labs, an AI startup, signaling a major strategic move in the AI hardware race.
The acquisition is valued at $8.2 billion, indicating a significant financial commitment by AMD.
This move directly intensifies the competitive landscape against market leader Nvidia in the AI sector.

stories.title: Here's what actually happened in OpenAI's Australian gov't server hack
stories.author: Kyle Orland
bullet_points: OpenAI experienced a security breach involving an Australian government server.
The attack allowed an agent to access sensitive data, including system information and source code.
The vulnerability was attributed to a lack of 'full set of safeguards' in the system.

stories.title: OpenAI says planned GPT-6.1 is too insecure to release
stories.author: Kyle Orland
bullet_points: OpenAI has reportedly shelved the planned GPT-6.1 release due to significant security concerns.
The decision highlights ongoing, unresolved security trade-offs within advanced large language models (LLMs).
This mirrors existing security challenges observed in current publicly available AI models.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the 'deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1' model on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized for text generation tasks, indicating its capability in language modeling.
Key associated technologies include transformers and safetensors, standard components in modern NLP.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline, indicating its application in generative AI tasks.
The model is associated with key ML technologies like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
It is categorized under text-generation pipelines and uses transformers and safetensors.
This indicates ongoing community interest and benchmarking of leading LLMs in the AI space.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, a 30B parameter open model, is now available via Ollama.
The model is specifically designed for autonomous agents capable of multi-step tasks and tool calling.
It is optimized to run locally on user hardware, emphasizing on-device AI capabilities.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a substantial developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved within Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through the implementation of Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent performance shows up to a 90% speed increase when benchmarked using Aider.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using the MLX engine.
The performance improvements translate to faster response times and higher quality model outputs.
The updated engine also demonstrates reduced memory consumption when running models.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, offering an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The key feature is the ability to run these AI agents locally on the user's own hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, facilitating local LLM deployment.

stories.title: AI researchers put out videos saying superintelligence is ‘exactly as dangerous as it sounds’
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: AI researchers are expressing significant concern regarding the existential risk posed by superintelligence.
The sentiment is highlighted by a former OpenAI/Google DeepMind employee stating the risk of human extinction is near 50/50.
The discussion is part of a broader series of interviews with leading AI researchers from major labs like OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic.

stories.title: Thinking Before Thinking: Scaling Agentic Inference Through Meta-Reasoning
stories.author: Anirudh Goyal
bullet_points: Introduces 'agentic meta-reasoning' to manage complex, long-running AI agent tasks.
Addresses the challenge of controlling execution flow (e.g., when to stop, what to build upon) in advanced agents.
Separates task-level computation (workers) from high-level decision-making (controller) for structured reasoning.

stories.title: Breaking the Uniformity Trap: Scaling Video Diffusion Model via SplitMoE
stories.author: Fan Tang
bullet_points: Introduces SplitMoE, a novel approach to scale video diffusion models using Mixture-of-Experts (MoE).
Addresses the 'uniformity trap' in visual MoEs, where independent token routing fails to handle spatiotemporal redundancy in video data.
Proposes a method to improve semantic organization and expert utilization in visual generative models beyond standard LLM adaptations.

stories.title: Imagine3D-LLM: Teaching MLLMs to Imagine 3D Scenes Before Answering
stories.author: Sunghwan Hong
bullet_points: Addresses the core limitation of current MLLMs: difficulty in reasoning about 3D scenes from multi-view images.
Introduces 'Imagine3D-LLM' as a novel approach to inject 3D awareness into Multimodal Large Language Models.
Contributes to the active research area of bridging the gap between 2D image understanding and coherent 3D world modeling in AI.

stories.title: From Routing Signals to Selective Review: Visual regrounding in MoE VLMs
stories.author: Nanyun Peng
bullet_points: Addresses a critical failure mode in Vision-Language Models (VLMs): target-absence grounding failure, where models answer questions about missing objects.
Proposes a novel framework that utilizes internal routing decisions within Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) VLMs for detection.
Offers an improvement over existing methods that rely on generated responses, hidden states, or uncertainty measures.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI platforms with local, open-source LLM ecosystems.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release brings significant performance improvements.
Enhanced GGUF model compatibility is now available via llama.cpp integration.
The update broadens model support across various hardware, augmenting the MLX engine on Apple silicon.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA is introducing Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new model.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: BMW’s revamped i3 boasts up to 468 miles of range
stories.author: Andrew J. Hawkins
bullet_points: BMW is relaunching the i3 as an all-electric four-door sedan.
The revamped i3 is built on BMW's new Neue Klasse platform.
The updated model boasts an impressive range of up to 468 miles.

stories.title: Suspected ShinyHunters leader arrested in the Netherlands
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: A 24-year-old Amsterdam man has been arrested by Dutch police in connection with the hacking group ShinyHunters.
ShinyHunters is known for high-profile cyberattacks, including those targeting Ticketmaster, Rockstar Games, and the FBI.
The arrest occurred shortly before the group claimed responsibility for recent attacks.

stories.title: Protesters gather at OpenAI’s DevDay
stories.author: Hayden Field
bullet_points: Protests occurred at OpenAI's annual DevDay event.
The core message of the protesters was a demand for 'People Over Profit' from Sam Altman.
More than a dozen organizations sponsored the rally outside the event.

stories.title: Most powerful obesity drug yet: People lost up to 25% of weight in trial
stories.author: Beth Mole
bullet_points: Retatrutide is a novel, highly effective obesity drug.
It functions as a triple-hormone agonist, mimicking GLP-1, GIP, and glucagon.
Clinical trials demonstrated significant weight loss, with participants losing up to 25% of their body weight.

stories.title: NASA has a Dragon dilemma, and there appear to be no good answers
stories.author: Eric Berger
bullet_points: The article discusses a complex operational issue concerning NASA's reliance on SpaceX's Dragon spacecraft.
It raises questions about the implications of SpaceX's operational decisions on NASA's mission goals.
The core conflict revolves around whether SpaceX's actions are driven by self-interest or necessity.

stories.title: This study looks at how and with whom connected cars share your data
stories.author: Jonathan M. Gitlin
bullet_points: Connected cars and companion apps expose users to numerous data trackers.
The study investigates the mechanisms and entities involved in this data sharing.
Highlights the privacy implications associated with modern automotive technology.

stories.title: Skill-Space Shooting for Autonomous Robot Policy Improvement
stories.author: Yang Gao
bullet_points: The research addresses the need for autonomous robots to improve performance in the real world without constant human intervention.
It proposes a method ('Skill-Space Shooting') to allow robots to learn and improve from experience autonomously.
The work relates to the trend of using foundation models to compose behaviors, but highlights the current gap in self-teaching capabilities.

stories.title: STEPQuant: When and Where Errors Matter in Delta-Rule Recurrent State Quantization
stories.author: Ying Wei
bullet_points: STEPQuant addresses memory bottlenecks in LLMs caused by large KV caches in linear attention mechanisms.
Directly quantizing recurrent states leads to significant accuracy degradation due to error propagation over time.
The study identifies that quantization error impact is dependent on both temporal persistence and spatial dimensions of the state.

stories.title: LeapQuant: Efficient Linear Attention with Accurate Recurrent State Quantization
stories.author: Ion Stoica
bullet_points: The paper addresses the inference bottleneck in linear attention models (like GDN and KDA) used in modern LLMs.
It proposes 'LeapQuant' to improve efficiency by applying accurate recurrent state quantization.
The research aims to reduce the computational cost associated with updating the fixed-size recurrent state while mitigating quality degradation from quantization.

stories.title: Beyond the Timeline: Augmenting Long-Video Memory with Grounded Entity Biographies
stories.author: Gang Hua
bullet_points: The research addresses a key challenge in long-video understanding: maintaining the physical identity of entities across extended temporal sequences.
Current methods struggle because chronological descriptions and text entities fail to resolve when different objects share descriptions or when the same object is observed in disconnected events.
The proposed solution introduces 'Grounded Entity Biographies' to connect events belonging to the same specific entity, improving question-answering accuracy.

stories.title: Learning Meta-Skills for Agent Harness Design in Test-Time AI4AI
stories.author: Heng Ji
bullet_points: The research explores 'test-time AI-for-AI,' focusing on how one AI (Builder) can improve the environment for another (Target) without retraining either model.
A novel concept, 'Meta-Skill,' is introduced to define reusable principles for when and what kind of support the Builder should provide to the Target.
The Builder learns these environmental construction principles by analyzing the Target's execution feedback gathered during the development phase.

stories.title: AdviSD: Learning to Advise Frontier LLMs via Targeted Multi-Turn Self-Distillation
stories.author: Sercan Ö. Arık
bullet_points: Introduces AdviSD, a method to guide large, frozen Language Models (LLMs) using a small, trainable advisor.
The advisor learns not only from task rewards but also from feedback derived from completed interactions.
The research investigates the impact of 'plausible corrections' on the advisor's learning, showing they can potentially limit learning in shared-parameter models.

stories.title: Stochastic World Models for Verifying Vision-Based Neural Feedback Systems
stories.author: Clark Barrett
bullet_points: The research proposes using stochastic world models as an improved surrogate for vision-based neural feedback systems.
These models aim to overcome limitations of current perception surrogates like GANs, which are often too large or lack verification tractability.
The core technical challenge addressed is creating a tractable model that accurately captures sensor observation variation for closed-loop analysis.

stories.title: How Local Mixing Encodes Relative Position in Global NoPE Attention
stories.author: Beren Millidge
bullet_points: The paper addresses the inherent position invariance of standard attention mechanisms in NLP models.
It proposes using local mixing layers to implicitly encode relative positional information, challenging the necessity of explicit encodings like RoPE.
This research contributes to the ongoing trend of developing more efficient attention variants, similar to SWA and gated linear attention.

stories.title: Skill-Space Shooting for Autonomous Robot Policy Improvement
stories.author: Yang Gao
bullet_points: The research addresses the need for autonomous robots to improve their policies in the real world without constant human intervention.
It proposes 'Skill-Space Shooting' as a method to enable scalable, experience-driven policy improvement.
The work touches upon the limitations of current agentic systems that rely on foundation models for behavior composition.

stories.title: Breakdown of Local Denoising as Semantic Speciation
stories.author: Xun Gao
bullet_points: The research investigates two distinct temporal dynamics in generative models: a 'speciation window' (semantic commitment) and a 'nonlocality window' (context window insufficiency).
The study explores the relationship between these two windows, motivated by their observed concurrence in frontier AI models.
A 'common cause' hypothesis is tested, leading to a mathematical proof regarding the necessary relationship between the nonlocality and speciation windows.

stories.title: STEPQuant: When and Where Errors Matter in Delta-Rule Recurrent State Quantization
stories.author: Ying Wei
bullet_points: STEPQuant addresses memory bottlenecks in LLMs by using fixed-size recurrent states instead of large KV caches.
Direct low-precision quantization of these recurrent states causes significant accuracy degradation due to error propagation.
The study identifies that quantization error impact is dependent on temporal factors, specifically how long the memory state persists.

stories.title: LeapQuant: Efficient Linear Attention with Accurate Recurrent State Quantization
stories.author: Ion Stoica
bullet_points: The paper addresses the inference bottleneck in hybrid LLMs that use linear attention by focusing on the recurrent state.
It proposes 'LeapQuant,' a method for efficient linear attention combined with accurate recurrent state quantization.
The research aims to reduce computational cost while mitigating the quality degradation typically associated with quantization in long-context models.

stories.title: A Spectral Theory of Distortion in LLM Graph Reconstruction: Sharp Bounds and Empirical Characterization
stories.author: Jianru Shen
bullet_points: The paper introduces a spectral theory to analyze distortion when Language Models (LLMs) reconstruct graphs.
It provides sharp bounds for the Wasserstein distance between Laplacian spectra using simple edge counts (net change and symmetric difference).
This offers a more nuanced, mathematically rigorous way to evaluate LLM graph reconstruction quality beyond single aggregate distances.

stories.title: Beyond the Timeline: Augmenting Long-Video Memory with Grounded Entity Biographies
stories.author: Gang Hua
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of tracking physical identity of entities across very long videos.
Current methods struggle to connect events involving the same object when descriptions are ambiguous or events are temporally distant.
Proposes a novel approach, 'Grounded Entity Biographies,' to resolve entity identity across long-form video data.

stories.title: Learning Meta-Skills for Agent Harness Design in Test-Time AI4AI
stories.author: Heng Ji
bullet_points: The research explores 'test-time AI-for-AI,' where one AI (Builder) optimizes the environment for another (Target) without retraining either model.
A novel concept, 'Meta-Skill,' is introduced to define reusable principles guiding the Builder on when and what support to provide to the Target.
The Builder learns these environmental construction principles by analyzing the Target's execution feedback from a development set.

stories.title: AdviSD: Learning to Advise Frontier LLMs via Targeted Multi-Turn Self-Distillation
stories.author: Sercan Ö. Arık
bullet_points: Introduces AdviSD, a method to guide large, frozen Language Models (LLMs) using a small, trainable advisor.
The advisor learns not only from task rewards but also from feedback gathered during completed interactions.
The research explores the nuanced impact of 'plausible corrections' on the advisor's learning, potentially limiting its ability to learn useful advice in shared-parameter models.

stories.title: Multi-Agent Flow Matching with Decoupled Generative Guidance
stories.author: Fabio Pasqualetti
bullet_points: Addresses a core limitation in generative modeling: the lack of formal guarantees that generated outputs meet hard constraints.
Focuses on the complex challenge of enforcing multi-agent constraints where requirements depend on multiple agents.
Proposes 'Multi-Agent Flow Matching with Decoupled Generative Guidance' as a solution to allow agents to guide themselves without needing simultaneous input from others.

stories.title: STEPQuant: When and Where Errors Matter in Delta-Rule Recurrent State Quantization
stories.author: Ying Wei
bullet_points: STEPQuant addresses memory bottlenecks in LLMs by using fixed-size recurrent states instead of large KV caches.
Direct low-precision quantization of these recurrent states causes significant accuracy degradation due to error propagation.
The study identifies that quantization error impact is dependent on both temporal persistence and spatial location within the state.

stories.title: Beyond the Timeline: Augmenting Long-Video Memory with Grounded Entity Biographies
stories.author: Gang Hua
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of tracking physical identity of entities across very long videos.
Current methods struggle to connect observations of the same object across disparate events.
Proposes 'Grounded Entity Biographies' to resolve entity ambiguity in long-video understanding.

stories.title: Pretraining Latent Information Feedback Transformers with Teacher Supervision
stories.author: Mor Geva
bullet_points: Introduces LIFT (Latent Information Feedback Transformer) to address limitations in standard Transformer LMs.
The core innovation is removing the feed-forward bottleneck, allowing deeper representations to feedback to shallower layers during pretraining.
This feedback mechanism aims to reduce the need for recomputing intermediate results and capture alternative continuations in language modeling.

stories.title: Learning Meta-Skills for Agent Harness Design in Test-Time AI4AI
stories.author: Heng Ji
bullet_points: The research explores 'test-time AI-for-AI,' focusing on how one AI (Builder) can improve the environment for another (Target) without retraining either model.
A novel concept, 'Meta-Skill,' is introduced to define reusable principles dictating when and what kind of support the Builder should provide to the Target.
The Builder learns these environmental construction principles by analyzing the Target's execution feedback gathered during the development phase.

stories.title: AdviSD: Learning to Advise Frontier LLMs via Targeted Multi-Turn Self-Distillation
stories.author: Sercan Ö. Arık
bullet_points: Introduces AdviSD, a method allowing a small trainable advisor to steer large, frozen LLMs using natural language advice.
The advisor learns not only from task rewards but also from feedback gathered during completed interactions.
The research explores the nuanced impact of plausible corrections on the advisor's future decision-making, particularly in shared-parameter models.

stories.title: LongHarness Bench: Stress-Testing Language Model Harnesses for Long-Context Reasoning
stories.author: Xi Ye
bullet_points: Introduces 'LongHarness Bench,' a new benchmark specifically designed to stress-test language model harnesses for long-context reasoning.
Addresses the limitation of existing evaluations, which fail to differentiate between modern long-context harnesses due to saturated accuracy.
The benchmark incorporates diverse retrieval strategies, including lexical and semantic search, to evaluate both effectiveness and efficiency.

stories.title: How Local Mixing Encodes Relative Position in Global NoPE Attention
stories.author: Beren Millidge
bullet_points: The paper addresses the inherent position invariance of the standard attention mechanism.
It proposes using local mixing layers to implicitly encode relative positional information without explicit positional encodings (NoPE).
This offers an alternative to traditional methods like Rotary Position Encoding (RoPE) used in transformers.

stories.title: AI Agent Governance on AWS: Block Agents, Prove EU AI Act Compliance
stories.author: sarvar_04
bullet_points: Demonstrates practical application of AI Agent Governance using AWS Bedrock.
Highlights capabilities like hard-blocking runaway agents and PII redaction across multi-agent systems.
Addresses the critical need for compliance, specifically referencing the EU AI Act audit trail.

stories.title: Count It or Compute It: When a Tool Returns Rows, the Models That Count Them Right Spend the Tokens
stories.author: xbill
bullet_points: The article highlights a critical, often-untested aspect of AI agent performance: accurately counting the output of a tool.
Models that process and reason through returned rows consume significantly more tokens (6x to 26x) compared to models provided a direct count.
The benchmark shows a clear performance gap, with reasoning models achieving higher accuracy but at a substantial computational cost.
